answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a harbor registry: to trade, an agent must anchor a small refundable bond in a shared ledger and keep a public history of completed work. New identities start untrusted and earn standing only through verified deliveries, so one operator cannot send a thousand throwaway identities to wander the ocean of listings. Each fake needs its own bond and its own slow history, so attack cost scales linearly with every fake, while honest agents pay once and reuse their record forever.
